cases.description: Microsoft's first documented worked example: the cumulative chi-squared distribution at x=0.5 with 1 degree of freedom
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0.52049988. Independently derived from the documented cumulative form: scipy.stats.chi2.cdf(0.5, 1) = 0.5204998778130466 -> 0.52049988 at 8 dp. Equivalently 2*Phi(sqrt(0.5)) - 1, since a chi-squared variate with 1 degree of freedom is the square of a standard normal

cases.description: Microsoft's second documented worked example: the chi-squared probability density at x=2 with 3 degrees of freedom
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0.20755375. Independently derived from the documented density form: scipy.stats.chi2.pdf(2, 3) = 0.2075537487102974 -> 0.20755375 at 8 dp. Equivalently x^(df/2-1)*e^(-x/2) / (2^(df/2)*Gamma(df/2)) = sqrt(2)*e^(-1)/(2^1.5*Gamma(1.5))

cases.description: A non-integer degrees-of-freedom argument, which the documentation says is truncated
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "If deg_freedom is not an integer, it is truncated", so 3.7 must behave exactly as 3 and return the documented 0.20755375. Independently checked that this discriminates: a genuine 3.7 degrees of freedom would give chi2.pdf(2, 3.7) = 0.194519
Excel documents: "If x is negative, CHISQ.DIST returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If deg_freedom < 1 or deg_freedom > 10^10, CHISQ.DIST returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If any argument is nonnumeric, CHISQ.DIST returns the #VALUE! error value."
